source_review.notes: Reviewed all ten references. Abstract correctness and algorithm/progress practice were checked against Herlihy-Wing and Herlihy-Shavit; reclamation/resource risks against Michael and Brown; synchronization evidence against David et al.; current atomic/progress API behavior against the C++ draft, Rust atomics, and Java 21 concurrency docs; and target qualification against current Intel and Arm documentation. Eight sources resolved directly, IEEE returned accepted metadata, and ACM denied automated retrieval for two publisher pages. Restricted pages support scoped bibliographic/result attribution only, not inaccessible quotations or details.

evidence: Definitions and Notation consistently defines hard requirements R_h, candidates C, evidence E(c,r), eligibility, benefit vector B(c,w), target matrix T, ownership O, cost/risk K(c), and material margin Delta.
The chapter distinguishes hard gates, preferences, semantic equivalence, target-qualified progress, resource bounds, measured benefit, ownership, and decision policy.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Checked conjunction/gate terminology, per-target quantification, unknown-versus-pass treatment, vector rather than false scalar cost, and noncompensatory safety language.

evidence: Recomputed a 30 percent improvement on a component consuming 2 percent of request CPU as an idealized whole-request gain below 0.6 percent before integration effects.

artifacts/snippets/CONPAR-060/report.json records only qualified_library eligible, mutex rejected for no_block, custom rejected for reviewed_proof, and selected eligible score eight despite higher ineligible scores.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The decision facts/scores are explicitly illustrative inputs rather than universal weights or product recommendation.

evidence: Eligibility is conjunction across every hard requirement and supported target; one false or missing conjunct rejects or narrows the candidate before preference comparison.
Benefit evidence requires semantic/environment parity, representative workload set, material margin Delta, and no violation of tail, fairness, resource, power, or lifecycle constraints.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The framework intentionally does not reduce organizational, maintenance, security, or safety risk to an allegedly objective total score.

evidence: Reviewed no hard progress need versus interrupt/priority contexts, one/multiple targets, hidden atomic locks, allocation/reclaimer/runtime blocking, wide atomics, fallback, low/typical/saturation/overload, and measurement noise.

Reviewed paused readers/debt, destructor context, thread exit, cancel before/after commit, close/drain, restart/unload, library wrapper unsafety, maintainer loss, canary rollback/migration, removal of legacy code, threat models, and high-stakes use.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Boundary analysis spans specification, progress, targets, resources, organization, measurement, dependency, rollout, lifecycle, security, and safety.

evidence: All candidates preserve one explicit contract or declare semantic differences; hard safety/progress/resource/target gates precede measurement; missing evidence cannot pass.
Complete-path progress includes allocation/reclamation/fallback; cancellation/close align with commitment; evidence is target/version-bound; owners, rollback, and reevaluation triggers remain.
invariant_checking.notes: Checked decision invariants across specify, enumerate candidates, gate semantics, qualify targets, bound resources, verify ownership, benchmark, choose, record, canary, migrate, rollback, reevaluate, and remove.

evidence: The gate proof universally quantifies required evidence across hard requirements and supported targets and rejects false/missing cases without compensation.
The benefit proof conditions measurement on passed correctness gates, comparable semantics/environment, declared workloads, material whole-system benefit, and preservation of all other constraints.
proof_review.notes: This is an internal engineering decision-proof framework, not proof that one candidate is universally best, a formal source implementation proof, economic forecast, or safety certification.

evidence: Atomicity, lock-free target support, complete-path progress, latency, throughput, fairness, resource boundedness, maintainability, security, and safety remain distinct claims.
Mutex, delegation, snapshot, sharding, library, custom lock-free, wait-free, and state-removal alternatives state their own changed obligations rather than a fixed hierarchy.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Requirement, theorem/proof, API documentation, empirical measurement, organizational policy, and named human review remain distinguishable.

evidence: python3 tools/verify_snippets.py CONPAR-060 passed the deterministic gate model with recorded Python version, exact stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit code.

The chapter requires differential/history/model, sanitizer/weak-memory, target code/capability, representative workload, stall/overload/fault/lifecycle, hardware-in-loop where relevant, canary, observability, and rollback evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The model proves no real candidate's safety, progress, benefit, ownership, target compatibility, maintainability, or deployment suitability.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed contract, hard progress, candidate set, semantic/progress/resource/ownership gates, fair measurement, conservative interpretation, buy-before-build, decision records, incremental adoption/rollback, and removal.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed target matrices, capability exposure, complete-path blockers, competent baselines, workload parity, debt/admission, wrapper lifetime types, dependency/owner plans, evidence versioning, kill criteria, quiescent migration, and reevaluation triggers.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet foregrounds gates before scores; exposition progresses from contract to evidence and lifecycle; the gate model is reproducible; ten examples are distinct; and five exercises progress from requirement classification to railway transfer with complete matching answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external concurrency-theory, formal-methods, performance, C++/Java/Rust, compiler, architecture, scheduler, product, economic, medical, railway, regulatory, operational, cybersecurity, or safety review is claimed. The chapter and model establish neither any candidate's source correctness nor linearizability, progress, target support, resource bounds, benchmark benefit, ownership, maintainability, security, or deployment safety.
